newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIAN DIES IN ISRAELI BRIDGE DISASTER
One Australian is dead and around 40 others injured after a bridge collapsed outside a stadium in Tel Aviv, Israel, where an international Jewish sporting competition is being held.
About 100 of the 370 Australian team members were crossing the bridge on their way to the event's opening ceremony, when it collapsed into a river.
One of the Australian team's media officers, Peter Scott, was on the bridge when it collapsed.
"I was standing right on the crack between two parts of the tried to untangle ourselves because we were scared that people would get so entangled they wouldn't be able to move," he said.

"For the first few seconds, nobody panicked and there were an awful lot of people. The Israelis were immediately in the water, they were helping people off, and once you got off the bridge - well you were in four feet of water."
Mr Scott said team members have been assembled at an emergency centre in Tel Aviv for a head count, while officials visit hospitals to check for deaths and injuries.
He said the Australian athletes are being provided with banks of emergency telephone lines to call relatives in Australia.
President of the Council of West Australian Jewry Ron Samuel has spoken to team members involved in the accident.
Mr Samuel said it has been confirmed the person who died in the accident was Australian.

"We believe that it was a 37-year-old man who died, we believe that he died of a heart attack. The games have gone on they continued with the opening ceremony as they would have done in any other occasion," Mr Samuel said.
But the Chairman of the World Jewish Congress, Isi Leibler, who is in Israel on a private visit, said he is outraged the opening ceremony continued while the search for bodies went on.

"What I'm quite appalled with is the decision by the organiser on the spot and I think it is a catastrophic blunder to have gone ahead with the opening ceremony and not to call it off," Mr Leibler said.
"On the one hand they've got activities for an opening ceremony and on the other hand they're looking for survivors in a river, you know it's one of those terrible things."
The event has now been postponed for a day of mourning after the accident.
The Foreign Affairs Department in Canberra says families wanting information about the accident can ring 06-261 1420 or 06-261 3305.
CARNELL CONFIDENT ABOUT DEMOLITION INQUIRY
ACT Chief Minister Kate Carnell is confident an inquiry into the old Royal Canberra Hospital building demolition will fully investigate all aspects surrounding the incident.
Twelve-year-old Canberra girl, Katie Bender, was killed and several others injured by debris from the implosion, at the weekend.
The inquiry will be led by former Commonwealth bureaucract, Noel Tanzer.
But ACT Oppostion leader Andrew Whitecross is not satisfied, saying the inquiry's terms of reference are too narrow.
Mrs Carnell said she believes the terms are broad enough to allow a fast and efficient investigation.
NRMA BOARD FIGHT HOTTING UP
The Motorists' Action Group has launched its bid for control of the NRMA board, promising to re-introduce rebates for insurance premium holders.
The eight candidate team said it is also committed to protecting unlimited low cost road service and stopping members' funds being invested overseas.
The group needs to secure five positions in the October election to stop the Nick Whitlam led faction gaining outright control of the NRMA board.
Motorists' Action Group President Richard Talbot says the NRMA can afford to reintroduce the rebate.
MINING INDUSTRY BRANDED GUTLESS
Australian conservation councils and environment centres have accused the mining industry in Australia of being "gutless" and lurking in the shadows of the native title debate.
A national conference convened by the groups has claimed the mining industry is the real winner from the native title debate, at the expense of other Australians.
Georgie Stewart from the Arid Lands Environment Centre in Alice Springs has just returned from the conference, which supported the struggle by indigenous people to protect native title rights.

Ms Stewart said: "The mining industry has an enormous amount to gain through this Wik debate. The shift with the Howard Government, or the push, is to significantly reduce the negotiating rights of native title holders on vacant Crown land, and to have no negotiating right whatsoever on pastoral leases."
"And for us, this is a big plus and a big win for the mining industry by downgrading...the Native Title Act, which essentially wasn't that much to begin with for native title holders," she said.
Ms Stewart said the conference recognised the importance of negotiated regional agreements as the basis for real reconciliation.
Ms Stewart said: "We've got attempts to push mining into national parks ... the broad community has only a restricted right to have a say in the mining industry as it is now.
"We see the exclusion of Aboriginal people from the process as yet another blow to the broader community's rights to have a say in the mining industry," she said.
"It's a big and powerful industry and we think they should pull their head out of the sand and come clean with the agenda on this debate."
DEMOCRATS TO FOCUS EFFORT ON TASSIE
The Australian Democrats have made Tasmania an electoral priority.

Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot, who has been in Launceston to mark the party's 20th anniversary, said the loss of Robert Bell's Senate seat to Greens Senator Bob Brown in last year's general election is reversible.
Senator Kernot said Tasmania will be a focus for the party, just as Western Australia was when the Democrats lost their Senate representation in that state.
She said a lot of effort, energy and resources will be allocated to future electoral success in Tasmania.
"There will be a steady procession of my colleagues and party people through here. We've been doing that and we believe that we can win back the Senate seat," Senator Kernot said.
